summary:
## Client Preparation and Comfort

Start by ensuring your client is comfortable. A small but significant detail is placing a pillow under the knees, which helps relieve pressure on the lower back during the treatment.

## The Multi-Step Cleansing Process

A thorough cleanse is the foundation of a good facial.

*   **Eye Makeup Removal**: Begin by gently but thoroughly cleansing the eye and lash area.
*   **First Cleanse**: Apply cleanser generously from the chest and neck upwards to the forehead. Use sweeping **effleurage** motions. Remove with hot water and sponges, rotating the sponges to always use a clean side.
*   **Double Cleanse**: This step is crucial for removing all impurities. Use **friction movements** to increase the temperature of the soft tissue, which helps break down and realign collagen fibers and increases tissue elasticity.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Always ensure your water is clean and you rinse sponges thoroughly between uses to avoid re-applying product or dirt to the skin.

## Exfoliation and Masking

These steps remove dead skin cells and provide targeted treatment.

*   **Application**: Apply exfoliator with a brush (or hands). It's a nice touch to warn the client that the product may feel cold.
*   **Treatment Time**: While the exfoliator or mask is setting, cover the client's eyes with rose water-soaked cotton pads and perform a relaxing hand and arm massage. This maximizes the client's relaxation and makes efficient use of time.
*   **Exfoliation Technique**: Use a **silicone exfoliating pad** in circular motions for a deep but non-abrasive cleanse. Follow up with your hands to get into smaller areas.
*   **Masking**: Apply a generous amount of the mask. Allow it to sit for about **8 minutes**, during which you can massage the client's other arm.

> [!TIP]
> If you have a facial steamer, the ideal time to use it is while the exfoliator is on the skin.

## Core Massage and Finishing Touches

This is the heart of the relaxing facial, followed by layering hydration.

### Massage Techniques

*   **Flow**: Strive to have your movements flow into one another without breaking contact with the skin.
*   **Aromatics**: Warm facial oil in your hands above the client's nose so they can enjoy the aromatic scent before you begin.
*   **Targeted Areas**:
    *   **Neck**: Use long, sweeping motions to release tension.
    *   **Jaw & Mouth**: Focus on straightening muscles to promote a youthful appearance.
    *   **Cheekbones**: Use sculpting motions to firm muscles and tighten skin.
    *   **Eyes**: Employ various techniques to help reduce fine lines and wrinkles.
    *   **Forehead**: Work on pressure points to release stored tension.

### Hydration Layering

1.  **Toner**: Apply after cleansing and exfoliating to remove any final residue.
2.  **Serum**: Gently pat a **Vitamin C brightening serum** into the skin.
3.  **Facial Oil**: Use as the medium for the facial massage.
4.  **Moisturizer**: Apply last to seal in the oil and provide additional benefits.
5.  **Eye Cream**: Finish with a targeted cream for the delicate eye area.

> [!NOTE]
> After the final rinse and before applying serums, gently blot the skin with a tissue to remove excess water, ensuring products can penetrate effectively.
transcription:
## Client Preparation and Eye Cleansing

Hey baby girls and boys. In today's tutorial, I'm going to be showing you how to carry out a relaxing facial and achieve beautiful, glowy skin using affordable products.

I'm going to start off by getting Bridie into the bed and making sure she's fully comfortable. I always like to place a pillow under the knees to stop too much pressure on the back area.

I'm going to apply some eye makeup remover to a cotton pad and cleanse the eyes and lashes, making sure all the area is makeup free.

## The First Cleanse with Effleurage

Then I'm going to apply four pumps of cleanser to my hands and apply this generously all over the face, remembering to work from the chest and neck up to the forehead. I mainly use effleurage techniques to ensure all the cleanser is worked into the skin. I repeat these movements around three times.

Using hot water and sponges, I squeeze out the excess water and begin removing the cleanser on the skin. I always like to rotate my sponges so I have a clean side to remove each area. If I feel my sponges are full of product, I rinse out with fresh water and repeat the removal until I am happy the skin is all clear.

## The Double Cleanse with Friction

I always like to double cleanse. This ensures all traces of makeup, oil, and dirt are removed, leaving the skin beautiful and clean. This time around, I use more friction movements. This increases the temperature of the soft tissue, breaking down and realigning collagen fibers and increasing tissue elasticity. I repeat these steps around three times.

I then remove again with hot water and sponges, always making sure my water is clean.

## Exfoliation and Arm Massage

After the skin is free from cleanser, I go in with an exfoliator. I like to apply my exfoliator with a brush, but you can use your hands if you prefer. I also like to warn my client that the product will feel cold. This will stop them from jumping and make the overall experience more relaxing.

I like to, after this stage, cover up the eyes with cotton pads soaked in rose water. This keeps your client's eyes closed and ready for a hand and arm massage. Some people may like to steam the face also at this point; this would be the perfect time. I don't have a facial steamer, but I still like the exfoliator to sink into the skin whilst I perform a hand and arm massage.

I begin my five-minute massage on Bridie's first arm. I also like my movements to flow into each other, so I try not to break contact unless it's to get another product.

## Activating and Removing the Exfoliator

Removing the eye pads, I then like to exfoliate the skin using a silicone exfoliating pad. I find these not too abrasive but still give me that scrubbed, fresh feeling of a deep cleanse. I work from the chest in circular motions all the way to the forehead.

I will then go ahead and use my hands to get into the smaller areas and ensure the face is fully exfoliated. I will then remove using hot water and sponges. I repeat this step until the face feels all smooth and free from product.

I have a few of Bridie's hairs popping out so I'm just going to adjust the headband.

## Toning and Mask Application

Applying some toner to some cotton pads, I then gently tone the skin, and also this makes sure I remove all the traces of the exfoliator.

My mask is then ready to apply. Again, starting from the neck all the way to the forehead, I like to use a generous amount, and using any leftovers for the chest area.

## Mask Treatment and Second Arm Massage

I covered the eyes using some fresh cotton pads soaked in rose water and begin the hand and arm massage on Bridie's other hand and arm. I usually massage this arm a little longer as I like to leave the mask on for around 8 minutes.

Once my time is up, I remove the mask using hot water and sponges, rinsing them out as many times as I need.

## Final Toning and Serum Application

I will then tone the skin one final time. I blot the skin with some tissue to remove any water sat on the skin.

I then use a vitamin C brightening serum and pat the product into the skin.

## Facial Oil and Advanced Massage Techniques

Warming the facial oil into my hands, I like to do this above the client's nose so they can smell the aromatic scent of the fig and mulberry. I begin the massage using sweeping motions of effleurage to the whole face to evenly distribute the oil.

Working on the neck, I use long motions to release the tensions Bridie holds in her neck.

I then work on the jaw and mouth area, straightening the muscles out for a more youthful appearance.

I'm just sculpting out the cheekbones to firm the muscles and tighten the skin.

Now working around the eye area, I'm using a variety of techniques to reduce fine lines and wrinkles.

I'm just working on the pressure points to release any tension Bridie holds in the forehead area.

## Moisturizer, Eye Cream, and Conclusion

I'm now going to apply the moisturizer to lock in the oil and give extra beneficial properties to Bridie's skin.

And lastly, I'm going to apply an eye cream to the eye area.

Thank you so much for watching this facial tutorial. I hope it was relaxing and informative for you. Please remember to like this video and subscribe to my channel so you don't miss any of my beauty tutorials. Thank you. Bye.
